papers.title_in_file: Deep Neural Networks as the Semi-classical Limit of Topological Quantum Neural Networks: The problem of generalisation
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results or main theorems, discussion or conclusion; proofs and appendices skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that views deep neural networks as the semi-classical limit of topological quantum neural networks, with an MNIST perceptron demonstration.

assertions.value: The authors report that their algorithm, which treats the perceptron as the semi-classical limit of a topological quantum neural network, obtains results similar to standard neural networks without the need for training.
assertions.anchor: Abstract, p.1; Section VI B, p.15
quotes: We apply a novel algorithm we developed, showing that it obtains similar results to standard neural networks, but without the need for training (optimisation).
we see that the results obtained are similar to the standard perceptron
assertions.certainty_reason: One numerical experiment on one dataset, run as a classical numerical approximation.
assertions.reader_inference: The accuracy figures sit in Table I, not in the quotes. The baselines are a hard-sigmoid perceptron and a softmax perceptron, each trained for a few epochs.

assertions.value: The authors state that the test uses the MNIST dataset of 60000 images of handwritten digits of shape 28×28, divided into training and testing sets with an 80-20 ratio, and that the standard perceptrons are trained for 10 epochs.
assertions.anchor: Section VI A, p.14; Section VI B, p.15
quotes: The MNIST dataset consists of 60000 images of handwritten digits of shape 28×28.
We first divide the dataset into training and testing sets with a ratio 80-20.
The two perceptrons are trained for 10 epochs, using categorical cross-entropy as the loss function.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup in Section VI A and VI B, p.14-15.

assertions.value: The authors state that the numerical approximations reduce the performance of the TQNN perceptron, and that direct computation of the weights is not computationally convenient in terms of accuracy with current technology because a quantum computer would be needed.
assertions.anchor: Section VI B, p.15; Section VIII, p.17
quotes: While the aforementioned numerical approximations reduce the overall performance of the TQNN perceptron
Still, one might argue that this is not computationally convenient in terms of accuracy, at least with our current technology, as we would need a quantum computer to achieve this result.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit in Section VIII, p.17.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract's no-training result therefore comes with an accuracy cost in the classical numerical version.

papers.title_in_file: The role of coherence theory in attractor quantum neural networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results or main theorems, discussion or conclusion; proofs and appendices skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that analyzes attractor (Hopfield-type) quantum neural networks as non-coherence-generating quantum channels.

assertions.value: The paper proves that after infinitely many iterations an attractor quantum neural network outputs the stored attractor that minimizes the relative entropy with respect to the input state.
quotes: After r → ∞ iterations, an aQNN outputs the stored attractor that minimizes the relative entropy with respect to the input state ρ
aQNNs are described by GIOs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Lemma 2 with proof, p.4.

assertions.value: The authors state that they consider only attractor quantum neural networks with maximal storage capacity, whose evolution is the generalized decohering map of their first equation.
quotes: Throughout this work, we will only consider aQNNs with maximal storage capacity, that is, those whose evolution is given by Eq.(1).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in Section 1.1, p.2.

assertions.value: The paper states, as propositions for the error-free case, that coherence cannot be used to enhance the performance of attractor quantum neural networks and that initial entanglement cannot be used to reduce their depth.
quotes: Coherence cannot be used to enhance the performance of aQNNs.
Initial entanglement cannot be used to reduce the depth of aQNNs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Propositions 6 and 7 (Section 2).
assertions.reader_inference: The conclusion notes that for the faulty networks of the maximally incoherent type an external source of coherence could give an enhancement.

papers.title_in_file: A general-purpose single-photon-based quantum computing platform
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results or main theorems, discussion or conclusion; proofs and appendices skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A Quandela hardware paper that reports a six-photon single-photon-based quantum computing prototype (Ascella) with gate benchmarks, a variational eigensolver, a three-photon quantum neural network classifier and Boson Sampling.

assertions.value: The authors report that they benchmark one-, two- and three-qubit gates on their device with fidelities of 99.6 ± 0.1%, 93.8 ± 0.6% and 86 ± 1.2% respectively.
quotes: we benchmark one-, two- and three-qubit gates with state-of-the art fidelities of 99.6 ± 0.1%, 93.8 ± 0.6% and 86 ± 1.2% respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: A company describes the performance of its own device.
assertions.reader_inference: The phrase state-of-the art is the authors' own description.

assertions.value: The authors report the first on-chip processing of 5 and 6 photons, at respective rates of 50 Hz and 4 Hz.
quotes: the first on-chip processing of 5 and 6 photons, at respective rates of 50 Hz and 4 Hz.
assertions.certainty_reason: A company describes the performance of its own device.

assertions.value: The authors report that the average total efficiency of the optical setup is about 8 %, including the single-photon source brightness, transmission of all optical components and detection efficiencies.
quotes: The average total efficiency of the optical setup is ∼ 8 %, including the single-photon source device brightness, transmission of all optical components, and detection efficiencies
assertions.certainty_reason: A company describes the measured efficiency of its own device.
assertions.reader_inference: A low end-to-end efficiency is what limits the photon rates reported.

assertions.value: The authors report that, for photon native computation, they implement a classifier algorithm using a 3-photon-based quantum neural network, and a first 6-photon Boson Sampling demonstration on a universal reconfigurable integrated circuit.
quotes: For photon native computation, we implement a classifier algorithm using a 3-photon-based quantum neural network and report a first 6-photon Boson Sampling demonstration on a universal reconfigurable integrated circuit.
assertions.certainty_reason: A company describes its own demonstration.
assertions.reader_inference: The classifier accuracy is split across layout lines in the body, so it is not quoted here.

papers.title_in_file: Learning interacting fermionic Hamiltonians at the Heisenberg limit
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results or main theorems, discussion or conclusion; proofs and appendices skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that gives a Hamiltonian learning protocol for fermionic Hubbard Hamiltonians reaching the Heisenberg limit.

assertions.value: The paper proves that the coefficients of the studied fermionic Hubbard Hamiltonians can be learned with total evolution time O(1/ε) and a number of experiments O(polylog(1/ε)), independent of system size as long as each fermionic mode interacts with O(1) other modes.
assertions.anchor: Abstract; Theorem 1, Section II A, p.4
quotes: The required evolution time across all experiments in our protocol is O(1/ε) and the number of experiments required to learn all the Hamiltonian parameters is O(polylog(1/ε)), independent of system size as long as each fermionic mode interacts with O(1) other modes.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1, p.4.

assertions.value: The authors state that the algorithm learns a more general class of fermionic Hubbard Hamiltonians than prior work, allowing complex hopping amplitudes and nonzero chemical potentials in addition to on-site interactions, and that it is robust to a constant amount of state preparation and measurement error.
quotes: we provide an algorithm to learn a more general class of fermionic Hubbard Hamiltonians at the Heisenberg limit, allowing complex hopping amplitudes and nonzero chemical potentials in addition to the on-site interactions
The protocol is robust to a constant amount of state preparation and measurement error.
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract states the scope of the protocol.

assertions.value: The authors state that the protocol uses O(N ) ancillary fermionic modes, where N is the system size, to obey fermionic parity superselection constraints, and name removing this ancilla overhead as a next step.
quotes: our protocol utilizes O(N ) ancillary fermionic modes, where N is the system size
A natural next step would be to find a Heisenberg-limited algorithm for our class of fermionic Hubbard Hamiltonians that eliminates the ancilla overhead altogether
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the ancilla requirement as a limit in the Discussion, p.19.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Advantage in Variational Bayes Inference
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results or main theorems, discussion or conclusion; proofs and appendices skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A theory and numerical-simulation paper that proposes quantum annealing variational Bayes (QAVB) and argues it has an advantage over classical variational Bayes inference.

assertions.value: The authors state that they show a quantum advantage of their quantum annealing variational Bayes inference over its classical counterparts.
quotes: show that there is indeed a quantum advantage to QAVB over its classical counterparts
assertions.certainty_reason: An analytic framework plus numerical simulation from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The evidence is an analytical framework and numerical simulation on Gaussian mixture clustering, not a hardware run.

assertions.value: The authors state that they apply QAVB to the clustering problem using the Gaussian mixture model and investigate two datasets in numerical simulations, and that ten datasets from the same generative model were used for the success-rate table.
quotes: we apply QAVB to the clustering problem using the Gaussian mixture model (GMM). In the numerical simulations, two datasets are investigated
Ten datasets were created by using the same generative model to create the dataset shown in Fig. 2
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their numerical setup in Section VI.

assertions.value: The authors state that the update equations of QAVB can potentially be implemented using ⌈log K⌉ qubits and O(K) operations per step.
quotes: We also show that the update equations of QAVB can be potentially implemented using ⌈log K⌉ qubits and O(K) operations per step.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors hedge the claim with the word potentially.

assertions.value: The authors state that existing QML algorithms can potentially speed up classical algorithms, but QML algorithms that outperform their classical ML counterparts are very rare or nonexistent.
quotes: existing algorithms can potentially speed up classical algorithms, but QML algorithms that outperform their classical ML counterparts are very rare or nonexistent
assertions.certainty_reason: An author statement of the state of the field, with no evidence given at that point.

papers.title_in_file: Inductive Construction of Variational Quantum Circuit for Constrained Combinatorial Optimization
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results or main theorems, discussion or conclusion; proofs and appendices skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A method paper that builds variational quantum circuits which output only feasible states for constrained combinatorial optimization, tested on a facility location problem in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in numerical simulations on the facility location problem, feasible and optimal solutions were found with a higher probability than with conventional VQE methods.
quotes: As a result, feasible and optimal solutions were found with a higher probability than conventional VQE methods.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one simulation study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the problem coefficients Ai and Bi,j were randomly sampled from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} and {0, 1, 2} to generate 100 instances, and that l-layer models (l = 1, 2, 3) were used as the conventional VQCs.
quotes: Ai and Bi,j were randomly sampled from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} and {0, 1, 2} to generate 100 instances, and optimization was performed using the proposed method and the conventional methods.
l-layer models (l = 1, 2, 3) were used as VQCs
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their simulation setup in Section V, p.8.

assertions.value: The authors state that one drawback of the method is the difficulty of applying it to constraint structures for which forwarding operations cannot be defined.
quotes: One drawback of the method is the difficulty in applying it to the constraint structures for which forwarding operations cannot be defined.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limit in Section VI, p.9.

papers.title_in_file: Adaptive measurement strategy for noisy quantum amplitude estimation with variational quantum circuits
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results or main theorems, discussion or conclusion; proofs and appendices skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A theory and simulation paper on estimating an amplitude under depolarizing noise of unknown intensity, using a variational circuit to adapt the measurement basis.

assertions.value: The authors report that they numerically show the proposed method can nearly attain the QCRB (quantum Cramér–Rao bound).
quotes: We numerically show that the proposed method can nearly attain the QCRB.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from simulation in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they prove the quantum Fisher information matrix is diagonal in their problem setting, so the QCRB of the amplitude parameter is not perturbed by the nuisance noise parameter.
quotes: we prove that the quantum Fisher information matrix is diagonal in our problem setting, meaning that the QCRB of the amplitude parameter is not perturbed by the nuisance noise parameter.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as the paper's first main result in Section III.

assertions.value: The authors state that the noise source is assumed to be depolarization with unknown intensity, and that the estimation error is close to the optimal bound when the variational circuit works well.
quotes: we study the noisy amplitude estimation problem where the noise source is assumed to be depolarization, but its intensity is unknown
The results show that the estimation error is close to the optimal bound when the VQC works well.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the noise model assumption and the condition on the result.

papers.title_in_file: Natural gradient and parameter estimation for quantum Boltzmann machines
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results or main theorems, discussion or conclusion; proofs and appendices skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that derives Fisher-Bures and Kubo-Mori information matrices for parameterized thermal states and quantum algorithms to estimate them, for natural gradient in quantum Boltzmann machine learning.

assertions.value: The paper states that its main technical results are exact analytical expressions for the Fisher–Bures and Kubo–Mori information matrix elements of parameterized thermal states.
quotes: The main technical results of this paper are exact analytical expressions for the Fisher–Bures and Kubo–Mori information matrix elements of parameterized thermal states (see Theorems 1 and 2).
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorems 1 and 2.

assertions.value: The authors state that their quantum algorithms for estimating the matrix elements involve a combination of classical sampling, Hamiltonian simulation and the Hadamard test.
quotes: our quantum algorithms for estimating their matrix elements involve a combination of classical sampling, Hamiltonian simulation, and the Hadamard test
assertions.certainty_reason: The algorithms are described without a numerical or hardware test in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that they plan to investigate the performance of the natural gradient approach numerically in future work, and that whether quantum Boltzmann machine learning suffers from the barren-plateau problem remains a pressing open problem.
quotes: and in future work, we plan to investigate numerically the performance of the approach.
it remains a pressing open problem to determine whether quantum Boltzmann machine learning suffers from the barren-plateau problem
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limits in Section VII, p.11.
